title: Why I Finally Turned Off My Notifications
script: Narrator: [honestly] For most of last year, my phone buzzed roughly two hundred times a day, and I genuinely believed that responding instantly made me a reliable person.
Narrator: [reflective] However, the more I reflect on that period, the more I realize instant responses had very little to do with reliability and everything to do with anxiety.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Even though every notification felt urgent in the moment, almost none of them actually required an immediate reply once I paused and looked closer.
Narrator: [tired] I would be halfway through cooking dinner, and a message would pull me away, so the rice would burn while I typed something forgettable.
Narrator: [determined] Eventually, I decided to run a small experiment. If a notification wasn't from my manager or my family, then it would simply wait until evening.
Narrator: [honestly] The first three days were harder than I expected, because I kept reaching for my phone out of pure habit, not actual need.
Narrator: [surprised] By the second week, though, something shifted. My mind felt quieter, and I noticed conversations at dinner instead of half-listening while scrolling underneath the table.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I also discovered that most messages solved themselves. People found answers elsewhere, or the question simply stopped mattering by the time I checked.
Narrator: [reflective] Despite what I used to believe, being constantly available never actually made me more helpful; it mostly made me exhausted and distracted from what was right in front of me.
Narrator: [warmly] Now I check messages three times a day, at set hours, and I tell people clearly so nobody assumes I'm ignoring them on purpose.
Narrator: [thoughtful] A few colleagues were skeptical at first, assuming I would miss something important, but nothing serious has ever slipped through in six months.
Narrator: [peacefully] As a result, my evenings finally belong to me again, instead of belonging to whichever app decided to interrupt them that day.
Narrator: [with a small smile] If someone had told me a year ago that silence would feel this good, I honestly wouldn't have believed them.
Narrator: [warmly] I'm not against technology; I just refuse to let it decide what deserves my attention every single minute of the day.

quiz.explanation: She discovered most messages solved themselves or simply stopped mattering by the time she checked.
